children: Michael Burry is doubling down on his bearish bets, adding to shorts in Micron Technology
as he questions the durability of the current semiconductor and AI boom. Burry said he made the latest short additions “in some size” in his September 22 Substack post.
Burry also added to his positions in QXO
, saying all five had "corrected tremendously" and that he found their prices “rather attractive.” He said all five are now "full positions" for him.

Burry’s latest bearish positioning comes as he highlighted comments from Acer CEO Jason Chen challenging expectations of a prolonged memory shortage. Quoting Chen, Burry wrote: “No way! How could there be a continuous shortage?” Chen said there is still a shortage of some components, including LPDDR5 and DDR5 9600, while Burry pointed to oversupply in DDR4, where Chen said there are “more sellers than buyers.” Burry added that Chen’s comments "align" with what he believes to be true.

Burry also took aim at the Nasdaq 100, describing the index as "historically overvalued" and "historically top-heavy" as it appeared poised to reach a new all-time high. He then pointed to Acer’s comments on memory supply, highlighting the possibility that rising production could eventually put pressure on prices.

title: Michael Burry adds fresh shorts in Micron, Nebius, Palantir as chip supply ramps up
